notesStmt.note: The date written at the bottom of a later draft of this poem (tex.00067) indicates that Whitman had begun the poem at least by July 1890, several months before he submitted it for publication.

This manuscript contains trial verses for the poem "Sail Out for Good, Eidólon Yacht," which was first published in the March 1891 issue of Lippincott's Magazine. There, it was grouped with three other poems under the collective title "Old-Age Echoes." It was later included in Good-Bye My Fancy (1891).

In perfect faith—in hope and trust— Depart!—hither no more no more ‸returning to these shores
Now, now ‸returning for good upon now upon thy great divinest venture

l.add: Spurning all thy yet known shores, seas, gravitation,
